body:
### Describe the bug

## Describe the bug

In 3.3.0, a dataclass in pure Python mode whose extension type is declared in an augmenting `.pxd` fails to compile as soon as any field has a **default value**:

```
params.py:6:4: 'max_depth' redeclared
```

The same code compiles cleanly on 3.2.9. Removing the defaults (leaving the bare annotations) compiles fine on 3.3.0, so it is specifically `name: T = default` in the class body that trips it.

This appears to be fallout from the new check added for #7246 ("Cython did not reject code with multiple contradicting type annotations on the same variable", listed under *Bugs fixed* in the 3.3.0 changelog). In `Cython/Compiler/ExprNodes.py`, `NameNode._analyse_target_declaration`:

```python
if not self.entry and self.annotation is not None:
    # name : type = ...
    is_dataclass = env.is_c_dataclass_scope
    # In a dataclass, an assignment should not prevent a name from becoming an instance attribute.
    # Hence, "as_target = not is_dataclass".
    self.declare_from_annotation(env, as_target=not is_dataclass)
elif (self.entry and self.entry.is_inherited and
        self.annotation and env.is_c_dataclass_scope):
    error(self.pos, "Cannot redeclare inherited fields in Cython dataclasses")
elif self.entry and self.annotation and env.directives['annotation_typing']:
    if not self.entry.scope.is_module_scope:
        error(self.pos, f"'{self.name}' redeclared")     # <-- fires here
```

The two branches above the new one both special-case `env.is_c_dataclass_scope`; the new branch has no such guard. When the field is declared in the `.pxd`, `self.entry` is already set, so the default-value assignment in the `.py` lands in the third branch and errors out — even though `object` (pxd) and `object` (annotation) are not contradicting types at all.

This looks like the same class of false positive as #7874 (`_Empty_Tuple: tuple[typing.Any] = cython.declare(tuple, ())`), which was fixed by carving out `is_module_scope` in that very `if`. C-dataclass scope needs the same carve-out.

### Why there is no workaround

The obvious alternative — declaring the fields only in the `.py` and leaving them out of the `.pxd` — is rejected by the other half of the compiler:

```
c.py:6:4: C attributes cannot be added in implementation part of extension type defined in a pxd
```

So for an extension type declared in an augmenting `.pxd`, 3.3.0 rejects the fields in the `.pxd` (because of the annotation) *and* rejects them in the `.py` (because they are C attributes). A cdef dataclass with default values is currently unexpressible in that layout. The only escapes are to drop the defaults, or to stop declaring the class in the `.pxd` at all and use `@cython.cclass` in the `.py` — which then makes the type uncimportable from other modules.

This also affects Cython's own dataclass decorator, not just the stdlib one — `@cython.dataclasses.dataclass` produces the identical error (see variant D below).

## Code to reproduce the behaviour:

`params.pxd`:

```cython
cdef class Params:
    cdef readonly object max_depth
    cdef readonly bint allow_multiple_copies
```

`params.py`:

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Params:
    max_depth: object = None
    allow_multiple_copies: bool = True
```

```console
$ cython -3 params.py

Error compiling Cython file:
------------------------------------------------------------
...
from dataclasses import dataclass


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Params:
    max_depth: object = None
    ^
------------------------------------------------------------
params.py:6:4: 'max_depth' redeclared

Error compiling Cython file:
------------------------------------------------------------
...


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Params:
    max_depth: object = None
    allow_multiple_copies: bool = True
    ^
------------------------------------------------------------
params.py:7:4: 'allow_multiple_copies' redeclared
```

The same two files compile without error under Cython 3.2.9.

<details>
<summary>Variants I checked</summary>

| # | Change from the repro above | 3.3.0 result |
|---|---|---|
| A | as above | ❌ `'max_depth' redeclared` |
| B | defaults removed (`max_depth: object`, `allow_multiple_copies: bool`) | ✅ compiles |
| C | fields removed from the `.pxd` instead, `cdef class Params: pass` | ❌ `C attributes cannot be added in implementation part of extension type defined in a pxd` |
| D | `@cython.dataclasses.dataclass(frozen=True)` instead of the stdlib decorator | ❌ `'max_depth' redeclared` |
| E | no dataclass decorator at all, plain annotated class attribute | ❌ `'max_depth' redeclared` |

B shows it is the assignment, not the annotation. C shows there is no place left to put the fields. D shows Cython's own dataclass support is affected. E suggests the check fires on any annotated class-body assignment whose name the `.pxd` already declares, dataclass or not.

</details>

## Expected behaviour

`params.py` compiles, as it did in 3.2.9, and `Params` behaves as a frozen dataclass extension type with working defaults.

More generally: when a field's `.pxd` declaration and its `.py` annotation are compatible (here both `object`), the annotated assignment should not be reported as a redeclaration. The docs state that "Dataclasses can be declared using the `@dataclasses.dataclass` decorator on a Cython extension type (types marked `cdef` or created with the `cython.cclass` decorator)" — a type marked `cdef` in an augmenting `.pxd` is exactly that case.

If the intent is to reject genuinely contradicting annotations, the comparison could reuse the `assignable_from` check that the `is_module_scope` branch right below already performs, rather than erroring on the mere existence of an entry.

## OS

Linux (Alpine, `python:3.14-alpine` in Docker) — also reproduced on Windows 11

## Python version

3.14.6

## Cython version

3.3.0 (regression from 3.2.9, which compiles the same code)

## Additional context

Still present on master as of `3292aa670301` — that region of `ExprNodes.py` is byte-identical to the 3.3.0 release.

Hit while upgrading a real project from 3.2.9 to 3.3.0; the pattern there is a frozen dataclass used as a parameter object, declared in a `.pxd` so other modules can `cimport` it and access its fields at C level.

Separately, and working as intended as far as I can tell: the new *"Declared container item types (e.g. `list[float]` or `tuple[atype, ...]`) are now used by the type system"* feature (#7288, #7798) also broke that project's builds, because `set[int]` in a `.py` annotation no longer matches a bare `set` in the `.pxd` (`Function signature does not match previous declaration`). Worth noting that the fix is not obvious from the error: the `.pxd` has to spell the item type using the new `cython.py_int`, since a plain `int` in a `.pxd` means C `int` and still will not match. A note in the changelog or migration guide would have saved some digging.
title: [BUG] 3.3.0: "'x' redeclared" for dataclass fields with defaults when the cdef class is declared in an augmenting .pxd
